memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "That day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug. They said, 'We've found water!' He called it Shibah, and to this day the name of the town has been Beersheba." - Gen 26:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the very same day that Isaac made peace with Abimelek, his servants come running with good news: "We've found water!" After all the disputes and dry seasons, God provides a fresh well right there in Beersheba. Isaac names it Shibah, and the place carries that memory ever after.

There is a lovely sense of timing here. On the day peace was made, provision came. It is as if God was quietly affirming that Isaac's path of trust and peacemaking was the right one. God's blessings often arrive after we have chosen the harder, better road of faith and reconciliation.

Water was everything in that land — it meant life, survival, a future. And after all the struggle, Isaac finally had a well no one contested. God had brought him from Esek and Sitnah all the way to abundant, peaceful provision.

Sometimes we cannot see how a long, difficult season will end. But God is faithful, and in His time He brings the "We've found water!" moments — the provision, the relief, the answer we had almost stopped expecting. Keep trusting Him through the dry stretches. The God who provided for Isaac still delights to meet the needs of His children (Phil 4:19).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I waiting for a "We've found water!" moment from God?
2. Can I trust God's provision even in a dry season?
3. How has God provided for me after a hard stretch of waiting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You provide in Your perfect time. Help me to keep trusting You through the dry seasons, confident that You will meet my needs. Amen.
